# Analyses of bundled event logs

Three analyses on the bundled datasets. The code below runs when this page is
built, so every table, figure and number in the text comes from the current
version of the package.

---

## Classroom · timing variants with and without a sender frailty

Juozaitienė & Wit (2024) compare *count* statistics with *timing* variants
(time since the most recent reciprocating or transitive event, continuous or
interrupted by a closing event). Count statistics also carry sender activity:
an actor who sends a lot accumulates large counts. A Gamma sender frailty
(`random_effects = "sender"`) absorbs activity differences between senders.

```{r classroom}
data(classroom_events)
specs <- list(
  count       = c("reciprocity_count", "transitivity_count"),
  continuous  = c("reciprocity_time_recent", "transitivity_time_recent"),
  interrupted = c("reciprocity_time_recent_interrupted",
                  "transitivity_time_recent_interrupted"))

no_re <- compare_models(classroom_events, specs, n_controls = 3, seed = 11)
no_re

with_re <- compare_models(classroom_events, specs, n_controls = 3, seed = 11,
                          random_effects = "sender")
with_re
```

```{r classroom-numbers, include = FALSE}
d0 <- setNames(no_re$delta_AIC, no_re$model)
d1 <- setNames(with_re$delta_AIC, with_re$model)
second0 <- no_re$model[2]; second1 <- with_re$model[2]
```

```{r classroom-figure, fig.alt = "Delta AIC of the three specifications without and with a sender frailty"}
cols <- c(count = "#d62728", continuous = "#2ca02c", interrupted = "#1f77b4")
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
for (tab in list(no_re, with_re)) {
  d <- setNames(tab$delta_AIC, tab$model)[names(specs)]
  bp <- barplot(d, col = cols[names(d)], ylim = c(0, max(d) * 1.15),
                ylab = expression(Delta * "AIC"),
                main = if (identical(tab, no_re)) "no random effect" else "sender frailty")
  text(bp, d, sprintf("%.1f", d), pos = 3, cex = 0.85)
}
par(op)
```

Without a random effect the count specification has the lowest AIC, ahead of
`r second0` by `r fmt(d0[[second0]])`. With the sender frailty the count
specification still has the lowest AIC, and its lead over `r second1` is
`r fmt(d1[[second1]])`. Among the timing variants, `r second1` fits better
than `r with_re$model[3]` by `r fmt(d1[[with_re$model[3]]] - d1[[second1]])`
AIC points once the frailty is in the model.

## Manufacturing · smooth effect curves

A stratified Cox model with `pspline(stat, df = 4)` on four endogenous
statistics, fitted on the first 30 days of the `radoslaw_email` dataset with
three controls per case. Statistics are computed with the default
`endogenous_features()` behaviour on case-control data: the controls are scored
against the history of observed events without entering it. Each time gap is
mapped to a recency weight with `transform_recency()` (1 for an event that just
happened, falling towards 0 as the gap grows), and a dyad with no such event
gets weight 0.

```{r manufacturing}
data(radoslaw_email)
re30 <- radoslaw_email[radoslaw_email$time < 30, ]
re30 <- re30[re30$sender != re30$receiver, ]

stat_names <- c("reciprocity_time_recent",
                "transitivity_time_recent",
                "reciprocity_time_recent_interrupted",
                "transitivity_time_recent_interrupted")

cc   <- sample_non_events(re30, n_controls = 3, seed = 11)
feat <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = stat_names)
for (s in stat_names) {
  w <- transform_recency(feat[[s]])
  w[is.na(w)] <- 0                     # no such event yet: weight 0
  feat[[s]] <- w
}

library(survival)   # coxph() recognises pspline() and strata() only unqualified
fit <- coxph(
  Surv(rep(1, nrow(feat)), event) ~
    pspline(reciprocity_time_recent,              df = 4) +
    pspline(transitivity_time_recent,             df = 4) +
    pspline(reciprocity_time_recent_interrupted,  df = 4) +
    pspline(transitivity_time_recent_interrupted, df = 4) +
    strata(stratum),
  data = feat, method = "breslow")
c(events = nrow(re30), actors = length(unique(c(re30$sender, re30$receiver))))
```

```{r manufacturing-figure, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "Smooth partial log-hazard contributions of the four timing statistics"}
panel <- c("reciprocity · continuous", "transitivity · continuous",
           "reciprocity · interrupted", "transitivity · interrupted")
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
for (j in seq_along(stat_names)) {
  s <- stat_names[j]
  rng <- stats::quantile(feat[[s]], c(0.02, 0.98))
  nd <- feat[rep(1, 80), ]
  for (o in stat_names) nd[[o]] <- stats::median(feat[[o]])
  nd[[s]] <- seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 80)
  pr <- stats::predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE)
  k <- grep(s, colnames(pr$fit), fixed = TRUE)[1]
  y <- pr$fit[, k]; se <- pr$se.fit[, k]
  plot(nd[[s]], y, type = "n", ylim = range(y - 2 * se, y + 2 * se),
       xlab = "recency weight", ylab = "partial log-hazard", main = panel[j])
  polygon(c(nd[[s]], rev(nd[[s]])), c(y + 2 * se, rev(y - 2 * se)),
          col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#1d4e89", 0.2), border = NA)
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey60")
  lines(nd[[s]], y, lwd = 2, col = "#1d4e89")
}
par(op)
```

Each panel shows one statistic's contribution to the log-hazard, with the
other three held at their medians; the band is ±2 standard errors. In this fit
the two continuous variants rise steeply from weight 0 (no reciprocating or
transitive event yet) and stay high, peaking for the most recent events. The
interrupted reciprocity curve stays near zero until large weights and then
rises; the interrupted transitivity curve is highest at weight 0 and below zero
for most of the range.

## CollegeMsg · first 30 days

The same three specifications on the first 30 days of `college_msg`, with one
control per case:

```{r college}
data(college_msg)
cm30 <- college_msg[college_msg$time < 30, ]
c(messages = nrow(cm30), users = length(unique(c(cm30$sender, cm30$receiver))))
cm <- compare_models(cm30, specs, n_controls = 1, seed = 11)
cm
```

The count specification leads by `r fmt(cm$delta_AIC[2], 0)` AIC points. The
datasets article shows the activity heterogeneity of this network (see the
actor-degree panel on the [Datasets](datasets.html) page); without a sender
frailty the count statistics carry that heterogeneity, so this table ranks the
specifications on activity as much as on dynamics.
